messages:
samir (sec-eng): Heads up — after the RBAC refactor merged this morning, I see the infra-service role picked up read access to customer-configs.*

jess (oncall): :eyes: Do you have an example audit entry?

samir (sec-eng): Pasting the relevant audit log (sanitized):

```
2026-03-18T09:12:43Z  principal=svc-infra@redwood.internal action=iam:read resource=projects/1234/customer-configs response=ALLOW policy_id=rbac-refactor-2026-03-18
2026-03-18T09:12:44Z  principal=svc-infra@redwood.internal action=secrets:access resource=kms://projects/1234/keys/customer-key response=ALLOW
```

maria (infra): That second line worries me — if the role can call KMS decrypt, we need to assume any cached tokens could decrypt customer blobs. Which policy change caused this?

samir (sec-eng): Found the merged diff. The merge script combined two role maps and a permissive entry accidentally expanded a glob:`roles:
  - name: infra-service
    permissions: [configs.read, logs.read]
  +  - name: infra-service
    permissions: [configs.read, secrets.decrypt, kms.decrypt]
`
(essentially a duplicate merge that kept the broader entry).

jess (oncall): Ok mitigation plan: 1) Revoke infra-service role immediately. 2) Disable any active tokens for svc-infra. 3) Start KMS key rotation for affected keys. I'll run commands now.

jess (oncall): Running: `rbacctl revoke-role infra-service --scope=global --reason="emergency:privilege-regression"`

deploy-bot: Action recorded: revoke-role infra-service by jess (oncall) @ 2026-03-18T09:15:02Z. Pending propagation to all clusters (approx 30s).

dave (sec-ops): Also revoke service account tokens in k8s and cloud: `gcloud iam service-accounts disable svc-infra@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and `kubectl annotate sa svc-infra redwood.io/disabled=true -n infra`

samir (sec-eng): Noted customers with activity in the window: cust-alpha, cust-zen, acct-8421. No obvious exfil logs yet but we should assume potential read access.

maria (infra): Starting KMS rotation for `projects/1234/keys/customer-key` with emergency policy; will create new key version and set immediate primary. ETA ~12m. Will also add deny binding to the old key for svc-infra.

carol (prod-support): If we escalate, ops wants a short customer message. Can someone draft a one-liner we can use if needed?

samir (sec-eng): Draft for ops: "We identified an access-control configuration error affecting a small number of service roles. We have revoked the role, disabled affected service accounts, and rotated cryptographic keys. We are investigating potential exposure and will notify if any customer data access is confirmed."

jess (oncall): Creating incident ticket and assigning follow-ups: - revoke propagation (jess) - token revocation checklist (dave) - KMS rotation + validation (maria) - forensic audit + scope (samir) - customer comms standby (carol)

samir (sec-eng): Forensic notes: pull audit logs for 09:00-09:20 across projects, snapshot VPC flow logs, and gather any service logs from infra pipelines. Also capture the exact PR/merge commit for the refactor (PR#3492).

dave (sec-ops): We'll also invalidate cached encryption contexts: `redis-cli -h audit-cache FLUSHALL` and bounce any long-lived workers that hold tokens.

maria (infra): Rollback option: we can revert the RBAC merge PR (PR#3492) immediately if propagation doesn't finish cleanly. Preparing revert PR now.

jess (oncall): Current status: revoke completed across 95% of clusters, svc tokens disabled, KMS rotation in progress. Creating postmortem stub in /incidents. Will update when rotation completes.

carol (prod-support): Copy of the incident text saved for ops. I'll wait for confirmation before any customer-facing message.

samir (sec-eng): After-action items to add to postmortem: stricter merge checks for role deduplication, CI policy lint to fail on expanded permission globs, and automated smoke test that exercises secrets access for roles.

jess (oncall): Thanks team. If you see any suspicious activity surface in the logs ping with tag `#urgent`. Closing thread for now; continuing incident channel tracking in the incident board."
